source.title: Training Dynamic based data filtering may not work for NLP datasets
source.authors: Arka Talukdar; Monika Dagar; Prachi Gupta; Varun G. Menon

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper excerpt, though some pages and tables are absent from the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests filtering of noisy NLP data and reports synthetic label-noise results, but its main challenge is to AUM filtering efficacy; it does not test memorization of completely random labels or the other listed training claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports synthetic-noise validation accuracy for SST-2 under 20% and 40% noise, with unfiltered, sieving, and flipping conditions. It does not report training error for these conditions. Other AUM results concern filtering mislabeled examples, not the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates AUM-based detection and correction of mislabeled NLP data. It invokes random-label memorization as motivation but reports filtering performance and validation accuracy, without measuring training-set memorization or the learning order of clean and noisy labels. These results do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that AUM identifies some mislabeled NLP examples, but indiscriminate filtering removes correctly labeled examples and relevant language information. They hypothesize that inter-class feature similarity and reliance on superficial features reduce AUM's efficacy.
record.recipe_differences: The study injects synthetic label noise into SST-2 and applies AUM-based sieving or flipping; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise percentage and filtering treatment change the reported validation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 reports SST-2 validation accuracy at 20% and 40% synthetic label noise: unfiltered 85.38% and 82.70%, sieving 85.94% and 84.26%, and flipping 85.83% and 85.96%. No corresponding training error is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AUM-based sieving or label correction can modestly improve validation accuracy under synthetic label noise in SST-2.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 reports that approximately 60–65% of noisy samples were filtered, alongside substantial removal of correctly labeled samples. Low AUM also occurs for correctly labeled examples in nondominant classes within similar-text clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low AUM imperfectly distinguishes mislabeled NLP examples from correctly labeled, difficult examples.

record.peer_reviewed: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: For the synthetic-noise results, the supplied text reports validation accuracy but not training error, uncertainty estimates, or a clean-label baseline in the same table. Several relevant figures are present only as figures in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: Table 5 reports validation accuracy after synthetic label-noise injection and filtering, but does not measure training fit or the chance-level test error named by V4. The V4 entry is tested_not_extracted because the reported accuracy alone does not establish the version's central training-fit condition.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed across corruption levels.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.

Perfect training fit across corruption levels and steady test-error degradation from clean labels to complete corruption. Validation accuracy at two noise levels alone does not establish this joint behavior.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's V4 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. Table 5 and the filtering results are already declared in rows_left_out or concern a different construct, so they do not require missing claim-result rows. The study's criticism targets AUM filtering, not the random-label claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks fit completely random training labels, achieve chance test error, or do so without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper reports test accuracy after synthetic label noise, but does not report perfect training fit, chance-level test error, or a clean-label baseline in the same table.
Whether explicit regularization is necessary or sufficient for fitting random labels or generalizing on true labels.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
